source: Authorized private BakAi 5.1.9 captures. Public samples use owner-requested fictional financial and identity values.
operations: Complete selected capture-derived records, with owner-requested fictional values and public-safe source lookup labels. Selection covers observed type/currency combinations, not a complete card statement. Complete account ledger records are retained.
sanitization: Amounts, balances, dates, merchant/product names, payment purposes and identifiers are substituted consistently. Signs, currency relations, matching transfer/refund sides, ledger totals, timestamp offsets/precision, field presence and record order are preserved. Zero/null values and bank operation/MCC/currency codes remain. All merchant, provider and technical location names are fictional. These values must not be interpreted as the original user history.
gaps: Rejected/expired authentication and native background scheduling remain unverified.
Offset-free account dates use the documented bank-time assumption.
No independent account/card timestamp pair or full historical own-transfer counterpart coverage.
authSource: Authorized private login captures; credentials, identity, challenge values and source lookup labels are public-safe substitutes.
historyLimitSource: Authorized read-only Visa KGS, Elcard KGS and Visa USD probes using the saved plugin session; bank date 2026-10-17 (UTC+6). All three six-calendar-month intervals with one preceding overlap day returned result 0 (254/6/30 rows). A six-month Visa request extended seven days into the future returned the complete response in history-limit.json. Shorter requests ending today versus seven days later returned identical complete operation arrays on all three cards (221/6/20 rows). An older short Visa interval also succeeded: the advertised limit concerns request span rather than a confirmed rolling retention cutoff. Exact maximum day count is not established; the plugin enforces the advertised six-calendar-month import period. Raw responses remain private under ignored local research.
